candidates.name: node:fs (writeFile to temp in same dir + rename)

evidence.claim: Already implemented privately in rules/build.mjs:54-59; 6 lines, zero dependencies.

The bounded EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES rename retry (win32 only, fixed attempts, backoff) is an explicit phase goal and is required; windows-latest CI validates it with a test that holds the destination open. It does not decide whether it is written.
npm view: write-file-atomic@8.0.0, ISC, one dependency (signal-exit), modified 2026-09-09 — maintained by npm.
Reference rather than adopt: the pack ships with zero runtime dependencies today and hooks have a 1 s budget; read its Windows rename handling when the retry is justified by CI evidence.
npm view: graceful-fs@4.2.11, ISC, no dependencies, last modified 2023-06-09.
Its Windows rename retry is the canonical prior art for the EPERM/EACCES case; it monkey-patches fs, which conflicts with 'no framework magic' (B-7). Read, do not depend.
Direct equivalent of the O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock in the source pack's record-progress.py; no dependency.
Not covered: stale-lock recovery after a crash. The source pack does not implement it either; do not add it unobserved.
npm view: last modified 2022-06-24 — unmaintained for four years; pulls in graceful-fs, retry and signal-exit.

Node docs, 'Spawning .bat and .cmd files on Windows': .bat/.cmd 'are not executable on their own without a terminal' and cannot be launched by execFile or by spawn without a shell. Resolving the shim path therefore does not help.
openspec's bin is bin/openspec.js in @fission-ai/openspec; spawning node with that file needs no shell and no quoting and is identical on all three OSes.
Covers Node CLIs only. git and docker are real executables and spawn by name; a tool that exists only as .cmd needs cand-007.

The phase goal ".cmd shim resolution under shell:false" is infeasible as written. Contract: spawnNodeCli(package, bin, args) and spawnExecutable(name, args); a .cmd-only tool is refused with a clear error. Goal text revision needs owner acceptance before plan.
npm view: cross-spawn@7.0.6, MIT, deps which/path-key/shebang-command, modified 2024-11-18 (the ReDoS fix release).

It solves .cmd by routing through cmd.exe /d /s /c with argument escaping — a shell, with the escaping risk that implies. The pack has no .cmd-only dependency once openspec is handled by cand-006, so the need is unobserved.
npm view: 12 direct dependencies. Too heavy for hooks with a 1 s budget and a zero-dependency pack.

candidates.name: @fission-ai/openspec as a pinned devDependency
candidates.fit_for_gap: spec backend: locating the openspec CLI

evidence.claim: Observed on this machine: openspec is installed under nvm's Node 24 while `node` on PATH is fnm's Node 26, so `npm root -g` from the running Node cannot find it. A global CLI is unreliable to locate even before Windows is involved.

A devDependency gives a fixed path (node_modules/@fission-ai/openspec/bin/openspec.js), a pinned version, and makes cand-006 deterministic. It is also the literal reading of the requirement 'include openspec natively'.
npm view: @fission-ai/openspec@1.13.1, MIT, modified 2026-09-17, engines node >=20.19.0. Installed and exercised here: 1.10.0.

maintenance.pin: 1.10.0 — the version that ran openspec init in this repository; upgrade as a separate change

evidence.claim: windows-latest / ubuntu-latest / macos-latest × Node 22 and 24 is the only available source of Windows evidence; the host runs Node 26 (non-LTS), so CI is also the only LTS evidence.
Blocked on an owner decision: the repository has no remote and the agent must not create or push one (A-16).

Required job steps: npm ci (the pinned openspec devDependency); node --test; node rules/build.mjs --check; node node_modules/@fission-ai/openspec/bin/openspec.js validate --all --no-interactive — the shell-free invocation, so Windows CI exercises the real path.

candidates.name: prometheus-knowledge-rs (pk) v1.8.0 as an optional native accelerator

evidence.claim: Verified by git ref at 01a1dbe: three Windows blockers exactly as reported — ungated std::os::unix import in pk-cli/src/main.rs:1216; File::open(dir).sync_all() in pk-store/src/prompt_snapshot.rs:171 and pk-learning-worker/src/main.rs:922; Command::new("npx") at pk-cli/src/main.rs:984. All other unix-only code is cfg-gated.
A 3-file patch was prepared in a scratch export (not applied to any repository). The Windows branch is unverified: no Windows target is installed here.
pk implements OKF v0.1 (writes `timestamp:` and string `sources`); OKF v0.2 renamed both, so 'latest OKF' requires a second, larger pk change.
`pk doctor` hardcodes the source pack's bash hook payload names (karpathy-hook-dispatch.sh …), so it reports failures against a Node-only pack regardless of platform.

SPEC.md declares Version 0.2. Required: frontmatter `type` on every non-reserved .md. New optional families: sources (mappings with required `resource`), generated {by, at}, verified [{by, at}], status draft|stable|deprecated, stale_after. Renames from 0.1: timestamp → generated.at; body '# Citations' → `sources` frontmatter. Reserved filenames: index.md, log.md.

§9 log.md is date-grouped, NEWEST FIRST, prose. The spec 'does not address time-series data, event streams, or append-only records' — so events.jsonl stays outside OKF and log.md must be a rendered projection, not an appended file.
The 20% not covered: OKF has no event model. The append-only JSONL stream and the idempotency receipts remain this project's own formats.

candidates.name: Sources registry + plain git clones under the user home
candidates.fit_for_gap: karpathy logs: project / personal / team tiers

evidence.claim: pk v1.8.0 has three hard-wired local scopes (pk-cli/src/main.rs:909-913) and no git, remote, team or per-project selection concept; Shared means cross-project on one machine.

Observed on this machine: ~/.prometheus/knowledge is a symlink into a private git repository whose last commit is 2026-08-23 with 35 uncommitted files — the personal tier exists by hand, is unmaintained, and relies on a symlink Windows cannot create without elevation.

Three registry files keep private repository URLs out of project repositories: .prometheus/sources.json (committed, team sources), ~/.prometheus/sources.json (personal, follows the developer), .prometheus/sources.local.json (git-ignored overrides).

candidates.name: sources-receipt.json checked by the KBD stage gate
candidates.fit_for_gap: karpathy logs: proving every selected log was read

evidence.claim: Nothing today records which logs a stage read. A per-phase receipt (source id, tier, resolved commit SHA, fetched-at, status) makes it checkable, and the previous receipt's SHA gives the update digest via git log old..new.
Not covered: proof that the model USED what was injected. The receipt proves selection and availability, not attention.

candidates.name: .gitattributes (text=auto eol=lf) + one CRLF-normalising reader in lib/platform + tolerant splitFrontmatter

evidence.claim: Probed directly: splitFrontmatter in rules/lib/render.mjs rejects CRLF input ("has no paths: frontmatter"); tolerance today is one untested line, readText in rules/build.mjs:18.
.gitattributes protects this repository only; OKF bundles cloned from team and personal repositories can still arrive as CRLF, so the reader must normalise regardless.
Not covered: files with mixed or CR-only endings. Unobserved; not handled.

candidates.name: node:os + node:path behind lib/platform (homeDir, tempDir, stateDir, join)

evidence.claim: os.homedir(), os.tmpdir() and path.join are the documented cross-platform primitives; no dependency is needed.

Enforcement is already mechanical: the blocking constraint no-home-or-tmp-literals matches $HOME, process.env.HOME and /tmp/ in every .mjs, verified against known-bad fixtures when constraints.md was generated.
Tests inject both roots, so no test reads or writes the real home directory.
